Reviewer: You (required).

Open Repositories and inspect application.ts and quality-policy.json (or any TypeScript and JSON files). Keywords, declarations, strings, comments and JSON keys/values now receive language-owned colors without a configuration file. Edit, select, undo and scroll; ordinary editing also remains available for unsupported files.

The implementation follows the agreed ownership:
- LspContributor owns discovery, shared instances, consumer/document lifetime, cancellation, stale results and the authenticated direct relay.
- TypeScriptContributor owns TypeScript applicability, project scope, the language server and its token/color rules.
- JsonContributor owns JSON applicability, scope, the Microsoft JSON service, token classification and color rules.
- RelationalUi consumes optional language support and paints the visible text while retaining native editing.
- Application/template composition enables these contributors and supplies configuration; it contains no copied LSP orchestration.

Review the attached screenshots and verification evidence. They cover real files, unsaved dependency changes, shared-instance cleanup, stale results, undo, scrolling and no graph operation for each edit.

Verification: repository type-safety and build checks passed. The full browser run had 346/358 passes before the final fixture and workspace-isolation corrections; all 37 targeted browser reruns passed afterward. The planning-save timing check and planning-navigation case also passed targeted reruns without changing their acceptance criteria. The original failed checkpoint is retained and was not rerun in full; see the attached verification note.

Known limit: JSON parsing/classification currently runs once per changed document version, not incrementally. The attached 2.12 MB / 56,940-line measurement records about 128 ms initial classification, 12 ms cached access and 108 ms after an edit on this machine; these are service-side measurements, not a UI latency guarantee.

Only coloring is exposed in the editor in this task. The next typed-function-signature task remains gated on your approval.

properties.description:
Implement this serial plan, with one item per contributor and application composition separate:

1. **LspContributor:** Own the reusable language-independent graph contracts, discovery and selection, server-instance management, LSP client/session machinery, and token-to-color provider mechanism. Factories and server instances are graph nodes. The instance manager coordinates creation, project-scoped reuse, consumer tracking and cleanup; the client synchronizes document versions, cancels obsolete requests, rejects stale results and preserves server provenance. After discovery and instance acquisition, editing traffic uses an established LSP connection. Where a server needs a relay, LspContributor supplies the minimal forwarding bridge through the existing host capabilities: no graph query, graph materialization or persistence for each edit. Color-provider selection and conversion can execute in the frontend. Contributor ownership does not force service-side execution.
2. **TypeScriptContributor:** Own TypeScript applicability rules, project-scope resolution, concrete server creation and token classification, including dependencies in other repository files. Register its server factories and token-to-color provider, with their applicability rules, through LspContributor when activated. All TypeScript-specific integration stays in this contributor.
3. **JsonContributor:** Own JSON applicability rules, project-scope resolution, concrete server creation and token classification. Register its server factories and token-to-color provider, with their applicability rules, through the same LspContributor contracts when activated. This separate language implementation proves the shared system is reusable.
4. **RelationalUi:** Own the reusable text-editor integration that requests language support and token colors through LspContributor and renders available results. Typing stays local; coloring updates asynchronously. Keep ordinary editing available without a server or color provider and preserve selection, scrolling and responsive incremental updates. The editor binding is part of RelationalUi and works for every template that uses it.
5. **Application composition:** Enable the four contributors and provide deployment-specific settings and existing hosting capabilities through their declared contracts. Contributors themselves install their factories, providers, relay handlers and editor integration. Templates contain no LSP-specific orchestration, forwarding, lifecycle, document-synchronization or coloring logic. Another template obtains the same feature by enabling these contributors and supplying supported settings, without recreating their behavior.

Token-to-color mappings are contributed implementations for this step. No color/theme configuration files or theme-file format are required. Completion, diagnostics and other editor features can use the shared system in later tasks.

Implementation decisions: reuse Microsoft's LSP protocol and JSON-RPC packages and typescript-language-server with the existing TypeScript tooling. Do not use the VS Code extension client. JsonContributor uses Microsoft's JSON language-service parsing information to distinguish property keys, string values, numbers, booleans and null, and supplies the token-classification output missing from the upstream JSON server. Include structural punctuation in coloring. Keep language-specific classification and color mappings in their owning contributors, and reuse existing hosting/transport capabilities. Declare only directly used dependencies in their owning packages. The other candidates from the earlier dependency inventory remain deferred.

Proceed directly with implementation and normal focused verification; do not add another POC or preliminary evaluation task. Keep the serial contributor tasks and the required human coloring review. Folding/unfolding is a separate backlog task.
